source.publication: 2025 AR1000F and AR1000NR Instructions (with the 2025 AR1000F return)
source.section: AR1000F lines 7A-7C, 8-25, 27-29, 34, 37-38 (Form pages 1-2); Instructions PDF page 12 LINE 7A (29 per taxpayer and spouse; 65 or over on January 1, 2026; 65 Special), PDF page 14 Standard Deduction table and LINES 26-29, PDF pages 30-34 Regular Income Tax Table (schedule 0% to 5,600, 2% to 11,200, 3% to 15,990, 3.4% to 26,400, 3.9% above, as settled in the record from the table), PDF page 11 item 8 (Social Security and Railroad Retirement exempt); PDF page 11 items 12 and 13 and the NOTE (total exemptions from all plans under 12 and 13 cannot exceed 6,000 per taxpayer); PDF page 13 LINE 18A and 18B (public or private employment-related plans, the recipient does not have to be retired; traditional IRA after 59 1/2); record ar_employer_plan_exclusion, ar_traditional_ira_exclusion_59_5; PDF page 8 Military Retirement Exemption; PDF page 10 item 1; PDF page 13 LINE 17 and LINE 18B (the military exemption uses up the 6,000 first); record ar_military_retirement_exempt

worked: Single, 60: U.S. military retirement 4,000 and a private pension 5,000. The military exemption is less than 6,000, so the remaining 2,000 may be taken on the private pension (PDF page 8). Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (primary) 35,000.00 + U.S. military retirement (primary) 4,000.00 + private pension (primary) 5,000.00 = 44,000.00. Federal taxable income = 44,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 28,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). AR1000F, filing status 1 (single); Arkansas builds its own income from lines 8-25, which here equals federal AGI less the exempt items. Line 8 wages 35,000.00. Line 17 U.S. military retirement (primary) gross 4,000.00, exempt in full (PDF page 8, PDF page 10 item 1, PDF page 13 LINE 17); not in total income. Line 18A (primary, age 60): gross pension 5,000.00 = 5,000.00; less the 6,000 exemption (the 6,000 is first used by the 4,000.00 military retirement exemption: 6,000.00 - 4,000.00 = 2,000.00 left, PDF pages 8 and 13): exemption = lesser of 5,000.00 and 2,000.00 = 2,000.00; taxable 3,000.00. Line 23 total income = 38,000.00; line 24 adjustments 0.00; line 25 AGI = 38,000.00. Projection check: federal AGI 44,000.00 - military retirement 4,000.00 - 6,000 exclusion (ar_retirement_exclusion_59_5_plus) 2,000.00 = state AGI 38,000.00. Line 27 standard deduction (filing status 1) 2,470.00; line 28 net taxable income = 38,000.00 - 2,470.00 = 35,530.00. Line 29 tax, schedule as numbers (0% to 5,600): 2% x (11,200.00 - 5,600.00) 5,600.00 = 112.00 + 3% x (15,990.00 - 11,200.00) 4,790.00 = 143.70 + 3.4% x (26,400.00 - 15,990.00) 10,410.00 = 353.94 + 3.9% x (35,530.00 - 26,400.00) 9,130.00 = 356.07; total 965.71. (The Regular Income Tax Table row 35,501-35,601 gives 967; expected keeps the schedule.) Line 7A boxes: personal 1 = 1 x 29.00 = 29.00; line 7C and line 34 29.00; line 37 total credits 29.00. Line 38 net tax = 965.71 - 29.00 = 936.71.
accepted_approximations: Arkansas builds its own income (AR1000F lines 8 to 25) instead of starting from federal AGI; the projection starts from federal AGI less taxable Social Security (exempt) and the reliefs here.

The schedule's bracket starts are derived from the printed tax table, which rounds the tax at each row's midpoint to the dollar; between rows and in rounding the projection's tax differs from the table.
